title: Audit: Provider Context Caching Public-v1 Policy Candidate
summary: Evidence-backed, provider-normalized public-v1 policy defining cloud and local prompt/context caching capabilities, Rig Relay control limits, privacy and approval requirements, usage evidence, cost/retention disclosure, and required future implementation work. Does not activate caching in production.

sections.content: This policy defines Rig Relay's posture on cloud-provider prompt/context caching ahead of the first public release. It covers automatic and explicit caching across all supported providers, establishes privacy boundaries, defines evidence requirements, and identifies what must be implemented before v1, what may be deferred, and what is prohibited until further review.
Disclose, do not pretend control. Provider-managed automatic caching must be disclosed and evidenced where observable, but Rig Relay must never claim control it lacks.

Refuse confidential context in explicit caches by default. Explicit cloud caching of confidential repository context is refused unless the user supplies recorded informed approval under a published privacy policy.

Public-safe context may use explicit caching. Public-safe or explicitly approved reusable context may use explicit caching where provider semantics are known and evidence records provider, mode, TTL/retention class, approval, and reported usage.

Local KV cache is not cloud retention. Local OMLX KV caching is modeled separately as local-runtime performance evidence, not as cloud retention. Local inference data never leaves the machine. Local retention policy (ttl_seconds=0 for disabled) provides the strongest privacy guarantee.

Stable prefix engineering for cache utility, not for retention. Deterministic context assembly should place stable reusable instructions and public context before volatile or privacy-sensitive request content only where that arrangement remains correct and policy-compliant. Context assembly must never increase retention of private content by accident.

sections.content: Recommendation for W2: Provider v1 Inclusion

W2 must decide which providers appear in public v1. Based on this audit, the following providers have sufficient cache/privacy evidence for v1 inclusion with appropriate disclosures: Anthropic (canonical evidence maturity), OpenAI (partial — disclose automatic caching and extended retention), and Local Inference (always safe). Gemini/Vertex AI require adapter work to extract cachedContentTokenCount and should only ship in v1 if that work is completed. DeepSeek requires independent cache behavior research before v1 inclusion. OpenRouter requires gateway-specific cache disclosure before v1 inclusion. Mistral was not researched in this lane and would require equivalent review before v1 inclusion.

rows: Were caches represented as uniform when they are not?
Each provider has a distinct row in the capability matrix with specific cache_mode, TTL, retention_class, and cost semantics. No uniform model is claimed.
Does policy claim control over automatic provider-managed caches?
Policy explicitly states rig_control_level=observe_only for OpenRouter and OpenAI automatic caches. Control is never claimed where absent.
Could confidential context be retained in explicit cache without informed approval?

explicit_user_approval_required=true for Anthropic and Gemini explicit caches. confidential_context_disposition=refuse_by_default or require_explicit_approval for all explicit cache modes. Principle 2 explicitly refuses confidential context in explicit caches by default.
Is local KV cache conflated with cloud data retention?
Principle 4 and the local_inference row explicitly separate local KV cache from cloud retention. Local retention policy (ttl_seconds=0 for disabled) is the authority.
Are cache savings based on actual provider usage fields?
Capability matrix maps each provider's exact API field names (cached_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cachedContentTokenCount) to Rig Relay's current extraction status.
Are pricing/TTL/retention assumptions current and official?
All claims cite official documentation URLs. Research date is recorded. Unknown fields are explicitly marked as null or unknown.
Is a v1 provider included without necessary cache/privacy policy?
DeepSeek is marked cache_support=unknown. The W2 recommendation section says it requires independent research before v1 inclusion. No provider is greenlit without evidence.
Was any live provider/runtime code changed?
This is a policy/schema lane. No rig_relay directory files were modified. Only docs/json/ and docs/schemas/ files were created.
Does remote publication support the exact policy claim?
Publication has not yet occurred. Must verify pushed SHA from remote main after publication.

sections.content: Rig Relay currently implements the following cache-related behavior across its LLM backend adapters (all in rig_relay/core/llm/backend/):

rows: Sends cache_control on system blocks and last user message. Extracts cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens. Beta header: prompt-caching-2024-07-31.
No 1h TTL. No tool caching. Only 2 of 4 breakpoints used. No cache_creation breakdown parsed. input_tokens semantic mismatch risk.
Inherits Anthropic cache_control behavior through class hierarchy.
No Gemini-specific caching. Inherits Anthropic patterns on Vertex, which has different caching semantics.
Extracts cached_tokens from input_tokens_details. Both streaming and non-streaming.
Does not send prompt_cache_key or prompt_cache_retention. No explicit cache control.
No cache control injection. OpenRouter gateway cache is opaque to the adapter.
Reads usageMetadata (promptTokenCount, candidatesTokenCount, totalTokenCount). Does NOT extract cachedContentTokenCount.
No cache extraction. No explicit cache CRUD. No implicit cache disclosure.
Deterministic block ordering (stable → dynamic → ephemeral). Prefix fingerprinting. Cache drift detection.
Prefix engineering only — no cache key injection. No multi-session block pool. No cache TTL awareness in layout.
Static adapter capability: Anthropic caching=true, all others caching=false.
Static. Not runtime-verified. Does not reflect Gemini/Vertex caching capabilities.
Per-provider truth table for cache_read/creation_verified and live_cache_evidence_preserved.
Gemini/Vertex marked as not verified. DeepSeek marked as not verified. No cache TTL or retention fields.
